description: Discrepancy in current medication dosages: furosemide dosage was increased to 60 mg daily as per last office visit and hospital discharge, but the home medication list in history section still shows 40 mg; not clearly updated prior to admission.
evidence_in_history: Current Medication List shows Furosemide 40 mg once daily; Office Visit #1 dated 2023-11-15 shows plan to increase furosemide to 60 mg daily.
evidence_in_summary: Discharge medications include Furosemide 60 mg once daily (increased dose to manage volume overload); Home medications listed as 40 mg but discharge meds updated to 60 mg.
suggested_correction: Clarify and update medication list to reflect furosemide dose increase consistently prior to admission and ensure outpatient records match discharge instructions.

description: No specific details or dates provided for diabetes educator referral or appointments between last office visit and admission; unclear if patient attended recommended outpatient diabetes education or endocrinology evaluation prior to hospital admission.
evidence_in_history: Office Visit #1 plan includes referral to diabetes educator and repeat labs in 3 months; Office Visit #2 mentions continuation of diabetes education and endocrinology evaluation but no concrete documentation of completed follow-up.
evidence_in_summary: Discharge summary mentions outpatient endocrinology appointment scheduled but does not confirm prior diabetes educator visit completion or interim monitoring.
suggested_correction: Include documentation of diabetes educator visits and endocrinology evaluations attended prior to admission; specify dates and outcomes to ensure continuity of care.

description: No recent potassium lab value documented at the time of admission or discharge despite history of mild hyperkalemia and the need for close potassium monitoring.
evidence_in_history: Lab results show potassium mildly elevated (max 5.0 mmol/L) in last 6 months; Office Visit #1 notes mild hyperkalemia 4.9 mmol/L with plan to monitor potassium closely with labs.
evidence_in_summary: Hospital course notes potassium was slightly elevated and monitored closely but no specific potassium values at admission or discharge labs documented.
suggested_correction: Include potassium lab values at admission and discharge explicitly in the summary to demonstrate monitoring and treatment decisions.

description: Discharge instructions mention patient's verbalized understanding of medication changes, diet, and fluid restrictions but no documented use of written materials or formal teach-back to verify comprehension.
evidence_in_history: Plans from office visits emphasize diet reinforcement and fluid restriction education but no documentation of patient education method or materials used.
evidence_in_summary: Discharge summary states patient verbalized understanding but lacks documentation of teaching methods or provision of educational materials.
suggested_correction: Document specific patient education methods used, such as written instructions, teach-back confirmations, or use of educational handouts to support patient comprehension.

description: No baseline or discharge measurement of urine albumin included in labs or discharge labs despite albuminuria importance in CKD and diabetes management.
evidence_in_history: Six-month lab history includes urine albumin (mg/g) values between 260-300 mg/g indicating albuminuria.
evidence_in_summary: Discharge summary recommends repeat labs including urine albumin in 3 months but does not document baseline urine albumin or discharge value for comparison.
suggested_correction: Include urine albumin values at admission and discharge to guide CKD and diabetes management and detect progression.
